empty.people: No one yet. Ramesh brings tea at 06:20.
empty.work: Nothing on the desk yet. He starts writing after breakfast.
empty.file: The file opens when he wakes.

segments.now: Before dawn. A bungalow on Tughlak Road, a letter on the side table, and someone about to wake for the first time in 195 years.
On the verandah with tea and four newspapers.
Walking the loop in Lodhi Gardens, among the tombs.
At home. Breakfast, then the Constitution of India, then his own notebook.
At Gandhi Smriti, on the Mahatma's birthday.
Khan Market: a stationer, a tailor, a bookshop, a grocer, and one refusal.
At home. Lunch, an hour of rest, then Ambedkar.
At the Gymkhana as Mr. Malhotra's guest, learning bridge.
At his desk. A first page for Berlin.
Asleep. The owl is writing up the day.

entries.text: Allotment letter, Directorate of Estates: one Type-VII bungalow, Tughlak Road, “in favour of Shri G. Hegel”. Found on the side table. Not delivered by post.
Woke under a ceiling fan with a letter beside me. The state found me before I found myself. In Berlin I would have called this the cunning of reason. Here it is apparently called a typing error.

Four newspapers on the verandah, two in a script I cannot read yet. I once called the morning paper the realist's morning prayer. Here the prayer is said in several languages, and I know the words to half of it.

entries.name: Ramesh
entries.role: caretaker of the bungalow for the Central Public Works Department
entries.text: Brought tea without being asked, and the news that the bungalow was meant for someone else.
Ramesh explains: the allotment was meant for Shri G. Hegde, Joint Secretary, transferring from Bengaluru. Somewhere between two desks, Hegde became Hegel. Status: under examination.
In the desk drawer, an envelope marked “Imprest, for incidental expenses”: ₹15,000. Every rupee will be accounted for. Let the state see how a philosopher spends.

My Berlin thesis, for the record: India is history's first morning, a spirit that dreams and never wakes into a state. I am drinking its tea in its capital, in a house its civil service gave me. I will keep the thesis on the desk, where I can watch it.
Walked through the tombs of two dynasties before breakfast, the Sayyids and the Lodis. People who only dream do not build their dead such houses. The thesis is shaken. Not yet fallen.

entries.name: Mr. R. K. Malhotra
entries.role: retired from the Indian Administrative Service
entries.text: Walks the Lodhi loop at a pace the Prussian infantry would respect. I said I think about the state. He said he ran parts of it for thirty-four years and the state never noticed either of us. Invited me to bridge at the Gymkhana at five.

The shelf holds the Constitution of India. Article 17: untouchability is abolished and its practice in any form forbidden. In my lectures, caste was the Indian order itself, fixed by birth like nature. Here a state abolishes it in one sentence. Either the sentence is idle or my lectures are. It will take more than a week to find out which.

entries.title: Phenomenology, Delhi supplement
entries.text: §1, sense-certainty. I wrote down: “Now it is 33 degrees.” By noon the truth had gone stale. Some things are the same in every city.
Today is Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday. The Directorate of Estates is closed until Monday. The error in my favour stands for three days.

Gandhi Smriti, the house where Gandhi spent his last days. Stone footsteps cross the lawn to the place where he fell. I put freedom into the state and its institutions; he began it in one person walking, spinning and refusing. We both wanted freedom made actual. His road was shorter, and he paid more for it.
Khan Market: civil society in a horseshoe, two storeys high. Half the shutters are down for the holiday; the other half sell what the first half would have. The system of needs does not close.

entries.item: Fountain pen and a bound notebook

entries.name: Masterji
entries.text: Forty years of Lutyens' collars in his head and a tape measure round his neck. He looked at my neck-cloth for a long time and said nothing, eloquently.

entries.name: Nidhi Rao
entries.text: Found in the bookshop holding my Philosophy of History, full of pencil. She asked whether I had come to correct the chapter on India. I said I had come to live here, and the correction would follow from that.

entries.note: The Prussian army should have had these.

entries.text: Asked the grocer for a bottle of wine. Dry day: no alcohol is sold on Gandhi Jayanti. I accept this as a matter of respect and record it as a sacrifice.

Ambedkar, 1936: caste is not a division of labour but a division of labourers. I described caste as nature’s determination. He describes it as a human arrangement, and what humans arrange, humans can undo. His is the more Hegelian position. I find this irritating, which is usually how I know something is true.
Message via Ramesh: Shri Hegde is in a guest house in Chanakyapuri and hopes the matter can be resolved amicably. So do I. I also note that possession is the first moment of property.
Bridge at the Gymkhana. It is whist that has acquired a constitution: bidding, contracts, and a dummy obliged to keep silent. Lost two rubbers. Understood the auction.
The sun went down over the club lawn at six. The light here does not dawdle.

entries.title: Depesche aus Delhi, Nr. 0
entries.text: First page drafted, for the readers in Berlin. The owl finishes it tonight.

entries.title: Hindi
entries.text: Two words learned: namaste and chai.

entries.title: Revision log
entries.text: Day one. “India has no history”: shaken, by the tombs, Article 17 and a tailor. “The state is the actuality of the ethical idea”: unshaken, though it lent me a bungalow by mistake.
Lamp out. The owl takes over.

depesche.title: Depesche aus Delhi, Nr. 0
depesche.text:
Readers in Berlin,

I write from a bungalow I do not own, on a road named after a sultan, in a city that has been a capital more often than Berlin has been a city. The Directorate of Estates allotted me this house by mistake. A Shri G. Hegde was meant to have it. Somewhere between two desks a d became an l, and the state, which I once called the march of God in the world, delivered me to Tughlak Road.

I woke at two minutes to six. By half past seven I had walked among the tombs of two dynasties. By half past nine I had read, in the Constitution of this republic, that untouchability is abolished. I have lectured more than once that India dreams and never wakes into a state. I am now drinking its tea in its capital, in a house its civil service lent me. You will understand that the lecture notes are under revision.

Note what has not changed. I still hold that freedom becomes real only in institutions. Today I watched institutions at work: a holiday that closes the Directorate and the wine counters alike, a tailor who measured my neck in silence, a club where the dummy at bridge is obliged to say nothing. Each of them is reason in a form I did not expect.

I have bought a pen, a kurta, a Hindi primer and a book by Dr. Ambedkar, who thinks more dialectically about caste than I ever did. I have spent ₹4,499 of the state's money and will account for every rupee.

Masterji will have my bandhgala ready on Thursday. The file will reach its verdict later. I expect to be corrected by both.

Your correspondent, for as long as the error stands,
G. W. F. Hegel

state.file: Under examination. The Directorate is closed until Monday.

theses.text: The state is the actuality of the ethical idea
